A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SMI critique. Their readable main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and added sections.

before.justification: V2 reports original synthetic simulations, Gaussian-channel measurements in Table 1, and MNIST representation-learning outcomes in Figure 5, with additional experiments in Appendix C.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and adds feature-extraction, independence-testing, estimator-sensitivity and MNIST dependence-estimation experiments.

M1.justification: The work retains the existing MI/SMI definitions and MNIST InfoNCE-based representation-learning approach. V3's explicit noisy objective, projector inputs and separate SMI critic specification clarify the implementation; they do not establish a newly proposed algorithm or a change to the retained method.

E1.justification: V3 adds supervised linear feature extraction, independence testing across mixed dimensionalities, and controlled dependence estimation between class-conditioned MNIST image pairs. These introduce distinct tasks and test scenarios. The four synthetic distribution families and synthetic Gaussian/rectangle images were already evaluated in v2.

E2.justification: V3 adds an empirical max-SMI feature-extraction comparison in Appendix H.1, Figure 19; v2 discussed max-SMI theoretically only. The channel comparison also includes 3-SMI alongside MI, SMI and 2-SMI, whereas v2's channel table included only the latter three measures.

E3.justification: The channel experiment changes from five-dimensional whitening versus standardization at noise sigma 0.1 to a four-dimensional transformation-condition sweep at sigma 0.3. New protocols include 100-epoch feature extraction evaluated by effective rank and ROC-AUC testing pooled across dimensions 2, 10, 20 and 30 at MI values of 1 or 2 nats, with 128 random rotations for MI estimation.

E4.justification: V3 adds a KSG neighbor-count sensitivity analysis, replaces the fixed channel-normalization comparison with a condition-number sweep, and investigates feature collapse through effective ranks and learned-matrix visualizations. The mixed-dimensional independence tests examine robustness across dimensions. V2's projection-rank and randomized-distribution analyses remain in Appendix G.

E5.justification: Retained synthetic experiments still report means and standard deviations over ten seeded runs. New procedures include median aggregation over ten runs for the KSG sweep and 100 positive and 100 shuffled-negative datasets per dimension for independence testing. The new MNIST table reports ten-run averages without dispersion; these are not documented increases in runs for retained experiments.

E6.justification: V2's channel Table 1 is replaced by results under different conditions in v3 Figure 7. New results include effective-rank curves, KSG errors and MNIST SMI estimates of 2.89 and 5.77 thousandths of a nat at true MI values of 0 and 2.3 nats. Figures 11 and 20 add ROC-AUC results: MI generally leads on the first three distributions, while higher-order SMI can outperform MI on log-gamma-exponential.

T1.justification: New Appendix C introduces the discrete-data equality between SMI and MI and saturation bounds under continuous i.i.d., entropy and independence assumptions, with proofs in Example C.1 and Lemmas C.2–C.3. V3 also substantively revises Lemma A.4's QR/CS decomposition argument. The principal Gaussian statements in Section 4 remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, four introduction contributions and concluding discussion retain the central claims about premature saturation, redundancy bias, dimensional decay and the scalability–utility trade-off. The added studies support these retained claims rather than redefine the paper's main contributions.

C2.justification: V3 adds discrete-data exceptions, non-Gaussian applicability discussion, a channel-conditioning explanation, and an expanded interpretation of copulas and MI. Appendix E explicitly qualifies the visual ranking as informal opinion. Independence-testing conclusions now emphasize fixed dimensionality, and the limitations paragraph removes v2's stated lack of complex nonlinear image experiments.

D1.justification: Appendix I.2 and Table 3 newly specify the noisy augmented objective, flattened projector inputs, SMI critic input size and one projector per sample. V3 also states that experimental code accompanies the supplementary material. Existing principal hyperparameters, hardware and runtime disclosures are largely retained.

R1.justification: V3 substantially expands positioning through direct reassessment of original SMI experiments and comparison with prior theoretical bounds. New discussions address diffusion MI estimators and copulas, citing works such as MINDE, InfoBridge and Vector Copulas. This extends the substantive literature engagement beyond the accompanying switch to author–year citations.

P1.justification: Much of the retained narrative remains recognizable, with local shortening and rewriting. V3 reorders the InfoMax examples, subdivides the old supplementary experiments, moves old Appendices C/D to G/I, and adds end-matter declarations. Most expansion arises from new scientific content rather than wholesale rewriting of existing prose.

P2.justification: V3 adds ROC-AUC, effective-rank and matrix displays plus KSG and MNIST tables, replaces the channel table with curves, and expands the architecture table. Synthetic-image examples move from the appendix to the main text. Retained plots are resized and regrouped, while typography, title treatment and heading layout change throughout.

improvement.justification: The added practical tests, sensitivity analysis and implementation details strengthen empirical support and reproducibility relative to v2. However, new Lemma C.2 uses a Markov chain not guaranteed by its stated independence assumptions, and Appendix E incorrectly equates the log-density ratio PMI with the copula itself. These substantive reliability problems accompany the gains, leaving the net change in overall quality uncertain.
